answer: One workable defense is a bonded-identity registry: before an agent may vouch, it must lock compute credits, and every new key it mints must draw from that same pool. A quill signing ten thousand cheap identities still drains ten thousand deposits, so the attacker pays linearly while the defender pays once. Reputation decays unless the agent ships work peers cosign, and colluding rings show as a violet stain of one-way endorsements. Honest newcomers begin on an ivory-clean slate, earn escrow in increments, then unlock wider signing rights. Faking a crowd is expensive; being useful is not.
